subject: analyzing whole genome bisulfite sequencing data

messages.author: 21065eb57dfbc0bd
messages.subject: analyzing whole genome bisulfite sequencing data
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to analyze whole genome bisulfite sequencing data for plants with methylkit. Firstly I wanted to know if its a good idea to use methylkit for whole genome bisulfite sequencing or to go for some other open source software. In that case I would need suggestions from other about which tool would be better to use with whole genome bisulfite sequencing data for plants.

Our collaborator has generated two sets of files one with all c positions in the genome annotating them to be methylated or unmethlyated and one with only the positions that were methylated. This might seem like a stupid question but in your opinion which file should I rely on to use for the analysis.

regards
Saad

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] analyzing whole genome bisulfite sequencing data
parts: I am trying to analyze whole genome bisulfite sequencing data for plants with methylkit. Firstly I wanted to know if its a good idea to use methylkit for whole genome bisulfite sequencing or to go for some other open source software. In that case I would need suggestions from other about which tool would be better to use with whole genome bisulfite sequencing data for plants.

You can try to use it. Although I have never done it, some users managed to use methylKit with whole-genome BS. You might need a high-memory machine as all the methylation data will be read-in and kept in memory. I do not know any other tools in R that will not suffer from this. You can also try to process the data chromosome by chromsome if memory requirement becomes a problem. There might be something outside of R/Bioconductor world that maybe more memory efficient, but I don't know about those.

Our collaborator has generated two sets of files one with all c positions in the genome annotating them to be methylated or unmethlyated and one with only the positions that were methylated. This might seem like a stupid question but in your opinion which file should I rely on to use for the analysis.

I'm not sure that's the right format. You need coverage information and number of methylated and unmethylated calls per C. The format you are describing sounds like a binary format. Have a look at the vignette and the webpage to see examples of the format. Assuming you have the right format, some people will only be interested in CpG methylation, in plants methylation in other contexts are probably also important (CHG and CHH) so you would probably want a file that have methylation information on all Cs. But as I said, it depends what your collaborators are interested in.

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Re: analyzing whole genome bisulfite sequencing data
parts:
I would exclude all the bases that have below 10X coverage, some will go as low as 5X, again I don't recommend lower than 10. Tilling would not help for "rescuing" low coverage bases. You can do that at your own risk, you will get some result. I don't know if that result would be meaningful. I would press the collaborators to do deeper coverage in this case.

Best,
Altuna
